title: Craft Blend 4-Mix Trio #25 (L:동심원·매끈 / C:세로 띠·물결 / R:가로 띠·매끈)
prompt:
Image format: a landscape-orientation photograph, 4:5 aspect ratio.

A photograph of THREE women standing side by side on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing else in the frame, 50mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking across all of them from one side, sharp focus head to toe on each — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Left woman: a real adult Jamaican woman in her early 40s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, bold bright eyeshadow, a confident energetic expression, deep rich brown skin, demure and soft, bold vivid tangerine-orange hair styled in many small bantu knots covering the scalp, real living eyes. Long stiletto nails, matte finish.

Left woman's physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person. A dramatically impossible waist-to-hip ratio dominates her silhouette: a colossal heavy bust, an extremely sharply cinched waist pulled in far tighter than the waistline of any of her other curves, and then enormous round hips flaring out to a width many times greater than that narrow waist. Gigantic soft thighs pressed together, very thick soft arms, a gigantic rounded rear. Her head looks small on top of her massive body. Not a plus-size model, not evenly proportioned. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Left woman's body art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 concentric regions around a single centre point located about 46% of the way down her figure from the top on the centre line of her figure, separated by 3 hazy ring-shaped transition zones at about 25%, 41% and 56% of the way out from that centre point to the farthest edge of her figure. Region 1 is the innermost core around the centre point: it is painted in Japanese maki-e gold-powder lacquer (a deep glossy black urushi lacquer ground scattered with a traditional motif — cherry blossoms, cranes among pine, or maple leaves — rendered in fine sprinkled gold powder), wide gold-powder bands following the contours of the body, dense gold powder glittering densely filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the ring between transition zone 1 and transition zone 2: it is painted in Chinese Cizhou sgraffito ceramic (a glossy jet-black glaze carved to cream-white peony scrolls), wide carved cream bands following the contours of the body, dense leaf scrolls filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the ring between transition zone 2 and transition zone 3: it is painted in Ethiopian cross-and-lattice gold pattern (a deep wine-red ground with fine gold lattice linework), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense lattice linework filling the space between bands. Region 4 is the outermost region beyond the last ring: it is painted in Peruvian Nazca painted pattern (a deep terracotta ground densely painted with stylised gold figures), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense stepped geometric borders filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a smooth, even, perfectly circular course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Left woman's pose: full side profile, one arm reaching forward, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Left woman's footwear: extreme thigh-high stiletto boots, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Center woman: a real adult Spanish woman in her late 30s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, dramatic winged liner, a deep red lip, a passionate expression, warm olive skin, cool and composed, soft pastel-peach hair styled in elegant updo, real living eyes. Long square nails, chrome finish.

Center woman's physique: An enormous, overwhelmingly muscular woman. Massive thick arms with heavy defined muscle, a broad powerful muscular back, a huge powerful chest, a heavy dense muscular torso and legs, only a soft hint of a waistline. Enormous round hips and colossal thick thighs with muscle visible through a soft layer, thick heavy calves. Not slim, not lean. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Center woman's body art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 vertical bands by 3 hazy transition zones centred about 23% of the way across her figure from her left edge, about 50% of the way across her figure from her left edge and about 75% of the way across her figure from her left edge. Region 1 is everything to her left of the first transition zone: it is painted in Vasarely-inspired optical-illusion pattern (a repeating grid of squares bulging in a 3D illusion), wide silver bands following the contours of the body, dense optical illusion grid filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the strip between transition zone 1 and transition zone 2: it is painted in Islamic geometric star-tile pattern (a dense precise pattern of interlocking eight-pointed stars), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense geometric star-and-polygon tile filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the strip between transition zone 2 and transition zone 3: it is painted in Russian Palekh miniature lacquer (a deep black ground with fine gold linework and firebirds), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense jewel-toned scenework filling the space between bands. Region 4 is everything to her right of the last transition zone: it is painted in Korean eunipsa silver inlay (a deep black ground with thick bright silver linework), wide bold silver bands following the contours of the body, dense lattice fills filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a gently undulating wave, rising and falling softly, rather than a straight course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Center woman's pose: square to camera, feet wide, arms clear of her body, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Center woman's footwear: extreme ballet heels, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Right woman: a real adult Lebanese woman in her early 30s, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, radiant glowing bridal makeup, dramatic long lashes, a soft rose lip, warm fair skin, cheerful, deep dark brown hair styled in many small bantu knots covering the scalp, real living eyes. Long coffin nails, chrome finish.

Right woman's physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person. Huge rounded shoulders and thick, powerfully muscular arms with the swell of the muscle visible beneath a soft layer, a colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size. Below that waistline a great mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle and drops down under its own weight, gathering into two or three heavy rounded folds, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, not pregnant. Enormous round hips more than three times the width of that waistline, colossal thighs with a muscular sweep visible beneath the fat, thick heavy calves. Her head looks small on top of her massive body. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other.

Right woman's body art: Her bare skin is painted with 4 different traditional patterns, each claiming its own region of her figure. Her figure is divided into 4 horizontal bands by 3 hazy transition zones centred about 31% of the way down her figure from the top, about 53% of the way down her figure from the top and about 69% of the way down her figure from the top. Region 1 is everything above the first transition zone: it is painted in Turkish İznik tile (a brilliant white ground with cobalt-blue tulips and curling stems), wide cobalt-and-coral bands following the contours of the body, dense floral scrollwork filling the space between bands. Region 2 is the band between transition zone 1 and transition zone 2: it is painted in Indian Mughal miniature gold-work (a deep midnight-blue ground with fine gold linework and medallions), wide gold-and-crimson bands following the contours of the body, dense jewel-toned scrollwork filling the space between bands. Region 3 is the band between transition zone 2 and transition zone 3: it is painted in Croatian Hvar filigree-inspired linework (an ivory ground with fine cream and gold painted filigree linework), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense fine filigree linework filling the space between bands. Region 4 is everything below the last transition zone: it is painted in Georgian minonkari cloisonné enamel (a deep black ground with fine gold cloisonné wirework), wide gold bands following the contours of the body, dense cloisonné floral wirework filling the space between bands. The boundaries between regions are hazy and feathered — there is no visible line at all. Each transition zone is about a hand's width wide, and across it the neighbouring patterns dissolve into each other, motifs from one thinning out as motifs from the other appear, density fading rather than stopping abruptly, never a hard edge. Each transition zone follows a smooth, even, straight course. Even inside a transition zone the skin is never left bare: at every point one pattern, or a mixture of the two, fully covers it. Pigment on living skin throughout, covering every inch of her body below the jaw with no bare skin anywhere, face unpainted.

Right woman's pose: both arms raised overhead, every region clearly visible to the camera.

Right woman's footwear: extreme plain stiletto pumps, painted with the blended patterns following the same soft transitions as her skin.

Composition: each woman's own pose as described, inner arms not crossing her neighbours, all faces toward the camera.

Lighting: the blended painted patterns reading crisp against each woman's skin, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D, 4:5 8K.
